Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 29-Dec-2025 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  FIFTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - DEC 2025/JAN 2026  
  SUBJECT: CSE 3124/CSE_3124 COMPUTER NETWORKS  
  (SPL: COMPUTER SCIENCE & ENGINEERING)  
  COMPUTER NETWORKS [CSE 3124]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                      Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1A)               Consider sending a packet from a source host to a destination host over a fixed route. List the delay (5)  
  components in the end-to-end delay. Which of these delays are constant and which are variable?  
  Justify.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
1B)               Using a timing diagram, illustrate and compare the interaction that occur in client-server             (3)  
  communication using both TCP and UDP.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
1C)               Analyze the devices in the network core and explain how it enables data to travel efficiently from a   (2)  
  source to a destination across the Internet.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2A)               The SSthreshold value for TCP Tahoe TCP station is set to 16. Initial CWND=1 and TCP starts with (4)  
  slow start phase and timer times out during 8 th RTT. Represent the problem using proper graph  
  and answer the following:  
  (a) CWND size during 3rd, 7th, 8th,11 th and 12th RTT.  
  (b) SSThreshold value at 5th and 10th RTT.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
2B)               Apply your understanding of TCP operation to describe how each of the TCP timers               (3)  
  (Retransmission, Persistence, Keep-Alive, and Time-Wait) function during connection management  
  and data transfer, using suitable examples or timing scenarios.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2C)               Discuss the importance of the following variables with respect to receiver buffer in achieving TCP (3)  
  flow control between sender A and receiver B LastByteRead and LastByteRcvd. Also, mention how  
  TCP controls overflow through these variables.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3A)               Assess the suitability of Link-State (LS) and Distance-Vector (DV) routing algorithms for large,       (4)  
  dynamic networks. Explain the advantages and limitations of each and conclude which is more  
  appropriate.  
  Page #1

Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
3B)   Consider the network shown as in Fig 3B. Suppose AS3 and AS2 are running OSPF for their intra-         (3)  
  AS routing protocol. Suppose AS1 and AS4 are running RIP for their intra-AS routing protocol.  
  Assume the ASes are configured to share external routing information with each other.  
  
  
  (a) How does router 3a learn about prefix x?  
  (b) Which protocol does router 3a use to distribute information about prefix x within the same AS?  
  (c) Router 4c learns about x from which routing protocol?  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3C)   Given a NAT-enabled router with a single public IP and multiple internal hosts, explain how NAT        (3)  
  handles multiple simultaneous outbound connections to the same external web server.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
4A)   An organization has been assigned the prefix 212.1.1.0/24 and wants to form subnets for four           (4)  
  departments, with hosts as follows:  
  (i) 75 hosts  
  (ii) 35 hosts  
  (iii) 20 hosts  
  (iv) 18 hosts  
  There are 148 hosts in all.  
  Formulate a possible arrangement of subnet masks to make this possible, and list the subnets in  
  CIDR notation. Propose what the organization might do if department D grows to 32 hosts.  
4B)   A sender sends the data: 11001100 , 10101010 , 11110000, 00001111. Employ a checksum                   (3)  
  mechanism and provide the transmitted message to the receiver.  
4C)   Show how the Count to Infinity problem may happen with distance vector routing and not with Link       (3)  
  State Routing. Use suitable explanations.  
5A)   Given the generator function G(x) = 1001 and the message function M(x) = 11010110. Compute the (5)  
  codeword. Consider that the codeword is corrupted, such that the receiver receives R(x) =  
  101110001111. Apply mechanisms to detect errors.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5B)   Demonstrate with a timing diagram how frames are handled when window size is 2m in case of Go          (3)  
  Back N protocol.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5C)   Outline the concept of vulnerable time. Analyze that the vulnerable time of slotted ALOHA is half of   (2)  
  that of pure ALOHA.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  
  Page #2
